I ported the card text formatter and rechecked Root's Unity flow test. Nothing was built or run (this session has no execution), so both parts are **NOT_RUN** and neither is a PASS claim.

**1. Flow-test recheck: CHANGES_REQUESTED**
- **R1, the strengthened test will crash:** `Transcript` (`RunMemoryFlowPlayModeTests.cs:47-48`) uses `graph["battle"]?["log"]`. When there is no live battle, the C# Run state still has a `"battle"` key holding null (`RunState.cs:84`). Newtonsoft turns that into a JSON-null object, so `?.` does not stop. Indexing it with `["log"]` throws.
- There is no battle right after creation, after each battle ends, at the finish and on reload. So the test errors at the first transcript check (L66). It fails loudly; it cannot pass falsely.
- **Fix (in Root's test file):** `var battle = graph["battle"] as JObject;` then `battle?["log"]`, and the same for `ev`.
- **F1–F4:** they look closed in the code, but none of the new checks has run yet, because R1 throws first.
- Three minor notes (N1–N3) are in the report and none blocks.

**2. Card text formatter, ported from `engine/rules-core.js` lines 100–201**
- The new file `core/MemoryForge.Core/BattleText.cs` has `BattleText.Card(BattleCardDef, BattleData)` and `BattleText.Op(EffectDef, BattleData)`.
- There is no type called `BattleEffect`; the real effect type is `EffectDef`, so `Op` takes that.
- **Coverage:** all eight lookup tables and helpers, all 39 effect types including nested `if`/`else`, plus every keyword (예약 전용, 계약, 성장, 소멸, uses), cost conditions and flavor text.
- **Matches JavaScript output:** the same truthiness rules, and `"undefined"`/`"NaN"` exactly where the JS would print them. Card and part names fall back to the id. `x/100` uses integer formatting, so it doesn't depend on how the runtime formats decimals.
- It reads only the definition it is given, so effective (upgraded or resonance) cards work the same way. No mutation, no randomness, no character stats.
- **Behaviour differences from the JS:**
  - Malformed definitions throw `ArgumentException` where the JS would throw a TypeError.
  - A missing effect type name returns `""` where the JS returns undefined. Both show as empty text where the JS uses it.
  - Lookups don't match JS built-in names such as `"constructor"` the way JS object lookups do.
